result.statement: S(f∘g)=(S(f)∘g)(g′)²+S(g). Every Möbius map has zero Schwarzian, and locally every C³ map with nonzero derivative and zero Schwarzian is Möbius. Hence S(M∘f)=S(f), with the indicated domain restrictions.

result.proof: For Brouwer, use arbitrarily fine triangulations of Δⁿ and the classical Sperner lemma: if a vertex on a face receives a label belonging to that face, some small simplex has all n+1 labels. If F has no fixed vertex, label each vertex v by an i with vᵢ>Fᵢ(v); such an index exists because both coordinate sums are one, and vᵢ=0 prevents that label because Fᵢ≥0. A fully labeled small simplex therefore exists. Let its mesh tend to zero and choose a convergent subsequence of its vertices using compactness.
